pr_title: stm32: sdmmc: Add IT mode and HW flow control
pr_body:
Fixes #39136

Convert existing SDMMC polling mode to IT driver r/w procedures.
Additionally, add a Kconfig option to enable HWFC feature.
pr_comments: @benediktibk Did you had a chance to test and see if  it improves things (even w/o DMA support)?

> @benediktibk Did you had a chance to test and see if it improves things (even w/o DMA support)?

Working on it
The download of 1MB via ethernet directly to the SD card is now successful, even with disabled hardware flow control (see comment in PR). Thanks a lot!

issue_context.title: SD disk access runs into TXUNDERRUN and RXOVERRUN of SDMMC driver
issue_context.body:
When using the SD disk access on a STM32H735 under load, the driver faults due to TXUNDERRUN (in case of writing to the SD card) and RXOVERRUN (in case of reading from the SD card) errors.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Activate ethernet
2. Start downloading stuff and write it immediately to the SD card

**Expected behavior**
The data should be written without any issues to the SD card.

**Impact**
It basically makes the disk access unusable in case there is any other load on the chip. The basic cause is in the HAL itself, which uses a polling mode to get the data out:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/hal_stm32/blob/5c8275071ec1cf160bfe8c18bbd9330a7d714dc8/stm32cube/stm32h7xx/drivers/src/stm32h7xx_hal_sd.c#L923

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - STM32H735G Discovery Kit
 - Zephyr Version fcb73bd4f68b0cf545591bf80328f79a4ea399bf


**Additional context**
I found a workaround for this issue. In the chip there is a hardware flow control unit available, which is disabled by default. Setting Bit 17 of SDMMC_CLKCR (HWFC_EN) activates this and then the issue is gone. Of course this is still not really a nice solution, as an active polling is pretty bad for the overall system performance. I suppose the proper solution would be to use DMA for read and write operations to the SD card.
comments:
@benediktibk Thanks for reporting this issue.
Due to the fact that Zephyr sdmmc driver is implemented using HAL which doesn't fit with Zephyr modularity and device model, adding DMA support requires to bypass Zephyr DMA driver. This is doable (STM32 QSPI driver has been implemented this way), but it is cumbersome.
To the opposite, adding IT support should be relatively straight forward. This solution isn't as nice as DMA support, but would at least avoid the polling, and would be a quickly available short term solution
Do you see an interest in this IT mode in the issue you're facing ?

EDIT: IT mode would be complementary to the flow control workaround

An interrupt based approach would definitely be better than the current polling. Technically I already have a rather whacky solution with the flow control workaround, but combining this with a reduction of the CPU load would be for sure a great improvement.

If it will be sufficient in the end for our project is hard for me to say, as the final IO load is not yet known. But I assume for most other projects this will be enough.
On top of that, I think enabling the hardware flow control by default in zephyr would be a good idea? Or am I a missing a possible issue with other usages?

> On top of that, I think enabling the hardware flow control by default in zephyr would be a good idea? Or am I a missing a possible issue with other usages?

It would be definitely a good idea. In a first step it could be added as a Kconfig option to limit risks (if any).

Regarding adding hardware flow control and enabling it by default, STM32F1 and STM32F4 (there maybe others) cannot use SDIO flow control due to an errata so this would not be a good idea for these SoCs.
